### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A14, A16, A17 and A18 no longer appear; they were present in about 20–30% of traces before (41, 51, 50 and 58 of 200 traces). [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- In the later window, activities A15, A23, A24 and A25 appear in all 200 traces; they were absent before. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- Before, A14, A16, A17 and A18 each led to A26; in the later window these activities have no outgoing edges because they are absent, while A15, A23, A24 and A25 lead to A26 and to each other. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR002, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- A41's successors changed from the old set (A14, A16, A17, A18) to the new set (A15, A23, A24, A25). [DIR009]
- A26's mean position moved from about 0.39 to 0.45 of the trace, and A41's mean position moved from about 0.33 to 0.29. [POS009, POS010]
- The lag between A41 and A26 changed from mostly 2 steps to mostly 5 steps. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process changed the set of activities executed between A41 and A26: in the later window, A15, A23, A24 and A25 are executed in every trace instead of A14, A16, A17 and A18, and A26 occurs later relative to A41 (lag increased from 2 to 5 steps). This is supported by consistent changes in occurrence, outgoing edges, relative order and position. A competing explanation that the new activities were always present but rare is unlikely because they appear in all 200 later traces and the old activities disappear entirely. [OCC001–OCC008, DIR001–DIR009, REL001–REL044, POS009–POS010, LAG001]
